text: As they line up, they're too high and too fast. With no engines, there's no second try. But Captain Bob Pearson is also an experienced glider pilot. He crosses the controls, one wing down and the opposite rudder, so the jet flies slightly sideways. The whole side of the plane hits the wind like a brake. It drops fast, without speeding up. The landing gear falls out by gravity. The main wheels lock. The nose wheel doesn't.
